Key points
• Dietary factors account for a large proportion of human cancers, particularly overnutrition that results in weight gain and
obesity.
• Evidence linking diet and human cancer began to grow in the middle part of the 20th century, and has become stronger and
more reﬁned with modern epidemiological methods, including case–control studies, cohort studies, Mendelian random-
ization studies, randomized controlled trials, and meta-analyses.
